method.window: from a start anchor in Y-1 to an exit in Y, named by Y = the Lunar New Year year
method.starts: 10-01, 10-15, 11-01, 11-15, 12-01, 12-15 of Y-1; the close of the last bar on or before the anchor
method.exits: before_lny = last trading day strictly before LNY; lny_plus_5 / lny_plus_10 = the 5th / 10th trading day dated strictly after LNY; feb_end = last trading day on or before the last day of February; mar_end = last trading day on or before 03-31
method.lunar_new_year: Hong Kong Observatory conversion table: the Jan-Feb date labelled 1st Lunar month
method.daily_rule: Y = 2009..2026 on daily bars; trading day = a daily bar of the file
method.weekly_rule: Y = 1981..2008; a weekly bar labelled Monday M closes on Friday M+4; each end = the last weekly bar whose Friday is on or before the daily-rule date on the Monday-Friday calendar (holidays not removed); lag_start_weekdays / lag_end_weekdays = Monday-Friday dates after the weekly close up to that date
method.return: end close / start close - 1, in percent
method.length: bars after the start bar up to and including the end bar (daily: trading days; weekly: weeks)
method.dip: lowest close among those bars / start close - 1 (closes only)
method.share_up: share of windows with end close > start close; Wilson 95% interval, z = 1.96
method.baseline: per cell and sample: every start bar from the cell's first window start bar on, held L bars (L = the cell's median length, a half rounded up), the hold ending no later than the cell's last end bar; overlapping, no interval
method.pooled: the daily 2009-2026 and weekly 1981-2008 windows of the same cell together (n = 46)
method.cross_cell: rank of (12-15, before_lny) among the 30 cells; the top cells and their other-sample values; Spearman rank correlation (average ranks for ties) of the 30 medians and of the 30 shares up between the two samples; no test
method.leverage: k x the XAUUSD return and k x the dip, k = 1, 2, 10; full notional k x the money put up, margin = 1/k of notional, closes only, no interest, financing, fees or spread; 10x half margin lost = 10 x dip <= -50% (dip <= -5%); margin gone = 10 x dip <= -100% (dip <= -10%), capped at -100%
method.passbook_spread: s = 1 - bank buys / bank sells on 2026-11-16; net = (1 + r) x (1 - s) - 1 per window, the same ratio at both ends, XAUUSD return for the TWD gold price
method.guard: a window is built only if its start close is at most 7 calendar days before the anchor and is not the series' first bar; a daily window whose series ends before the exit is not built
method.controls: (12-15, before_lny) per-year returns equal to RS-XAUUSD-20261115-001 within 1e-9 points with the same dates, daily and weekly; (12-01, before_lny) counts and medians equal to its 12-01 robustness; pooled (12-15, before_lny) = 27 of 46

limitations: Descriptive only: 30 start/exit cells, no test between them; the cells share years and overlap in days, so the best-looking cell is partly luck and is not a recommendation.
The (12-15, before LNY) and (12-01, before LNY) cells were published before registration; month-level statistics of October to March were known from RS-MULTI-20260901-001.
1981-2008 uses weekly closes: every end can sit some trading days earlier than the daily rule (max_lag_* per cell) and dips between Fridays are not seen.
Pooled 46 mixes daily and weekly windows.
Leverage is k x the close-to-close move: no intraday lows, financing, fees or spread; 2x is not a leveraged ETF's NAV.

The passbook spread is one day's Bank of Taiwan quote applied at both ends, and the TWD gold price is replaced by XAUUSD (USD/TWD ignored); the history rows were transcribed from a rendered page, not saved byte for byte.
The context sources describe physical demand; none of them is a price study, and this study does not test a cause.
No independent local source checks the weekly closes before 2013.

context_sources.quote: With the Chinese New Year (CNY) holiday approaching (15 to 23 February), both gold jewellery demand and bullion investment may improve supported by self-rewarding and gifting-related purchases.

In addition, gold bars and coins also attracted tremendous attention during the holiday as many retail investors took advantage of the local gold price dip ahead of the festival to enter the market for gifting and long-term saving.
Jewellers remain cautiously optimistic that the ongoing wedding season (November–March) will boost jewellery sales, given the expected large number of weddings.
In October, gold imports rose to $7.13bn from $4.39bn in the previous month, reflecting the seasonal uptick in demand for festivals and weddings.
